title: ASSIGNMENT – 5
subtitle: Simulation of ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) Using Socket Programming
name: Srikrishna O S

sections.heading: AIM
paragraph: To simulate the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) using socket programming. The server acts as a host or router: it enters the packet details (source IP, source MAC, destination IP and 16-bit data), develops an ARP Request packet containing SourceIP | SourceMAC | DestinationIP, broadcasts it to all connected clients, and waits for an ARP Reply. When a reply carrying the Destination MAC address arrives, the server sends the packet to the matching destination with the format SourceIP | SourceMAC | DestinationIP | DestinationMAC | 16-bit data.

The client enters its own IP and MAC address. When an ARP Request is received it checks whether the Destination IP is its own IP; if not it stays silent, if yes it replies with SourceIP | SourceMAC | DestinationIP | DestinationMAC and then receives and displays the packet from the server. The validity of IP and MAC addresses is checked before any packet is processed.

sections.heading: ALGORITHM
bullets: SERVER: validate destination IP, source IP, source MAC and 16-bit data.
SERVER: accept three clients, develop the ARP Request packet and broadcast it.
SERVER: poll for an ARP Reply, print the destination MAC and send the packet to it.
CLIENT: enter own IP and MAC; read the ARP Request and compare Destination IP with own IP.
CLIENT: if the IP matches, send the ARP Reply and display the packet from the server.
CLIENT: if the IP does not match, stay silent and send no reply.

rows: Server checks IP format (0-255 per octet) and MAC format (XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX)
Invalid IP 999.999.999.999 rejected before any broadcast
Router server accepts three clients on 127.0.0.1:5007
Packet 123.128.34.56 | AF-45-E5-00-97-12 | 155.157.65.128 developed and broadcast to all clients
All three clients received the request
Clients 1 and 3 compared the destination IP with their own IP
Both printed "IP address does not match." and stayed silent
ARP Reply with MAC 45-DA-62-21-1A-B2 sent to the server
Server sent the packet to the replying client with the destination MAC appended

sections.heading: LEARNING OUTCOMES
bullets: I broadcast an ARP request from a router server to all connected clients.
I implemented the client-side IP match check with silent behaviour for other hosts.
I delivered the packet only after the destination MAC was resolved.
I validated IP and MAC formats before processing any packet.
I observed that all clients must be connected before the broadcast.
